title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_55f
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor. The malware is known to establish command and control (C2) communication and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to identify and contain this threat within the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor. The malware is known to establish command and control (C2) communication and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to identify and contain this threat within the network.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the credentials username: analyst, password: Analyst123.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the credentials username: analyst, password: Analyst123.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target system, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`. Look for any services that are not part of the standard system services. In this case, the suspicious service is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by identifying all running services on the system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any services that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Now that you've identified a suspicious service, investigate its network activity. Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication.
levels.solution: To investigate the network activity of the suspicious service, you can use the command `ss -tulnp | grep bkd.service`. This will show you the network connections associated with the service. In this case, the suspicious port is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the network connections associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp | grep bkd.service` to list network connections for the service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual or unexpected ports being used by the service.

levels.title: C2 Containment
levels.content: Based on your findings, implement containment measures to block communication between the compromised host and the external command-and-control server.
levels.solution: To contain the threat, you can use the command `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j DROP`. This will block all incoming TCP traffic on port 80, effectively preventing the C2 communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider using the system's firewall to block the identified port.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j DROP` to block the port.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Verify the rule has been added by checking the firewall rules with `iptables -L -n`.
